QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_49

question.text: AIFs are required to bring an 'Investor Charter' to the notice of their investors. Which of the following BEST describes the Investor Charter?

answer.text: A confidential internal compliance checklist reviewed only by the Trustee.
A document with details of services provided to investors, grievance redressal mechanism and responsibilities of investors, collated in one single place for ease of reference.
A marketing brochure prepared by distributors for client acquisition.
An investor vote-counting register for LP resolutions.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 12: 'AIFs are required to bring an Investor Charter to the notice of their investors ... This Investor Charter is a document with details of services provided to investors, details of grievance redressal mechanism and responsibilities of the investors at one single place, for ease of reference.' **The Trap:** Options A, C, D are plausible-sounding but not the Investor Charter. The Charter is a public, investor-facing document, not a confidential checklist or marketing brochure. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C covers the same definition. Similar charters exist across SEBI intermediaries (stock brokers, MFs) — XIX-A may test the AIF Charter from the distributor-education angle. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Post the Investor Charter on your AIF website (even though marketing is restricted) and include it in every subscription booklet. It signals governance maturity to onboarding LPs.
